issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents should have signature addGuestStudents(int, String) (an int and a String reason), but the solution implements addGuestStudents with only a single int parameter. This parameter mismatch means the solution contradicts the specified API and would confuse students about the required method signature and how to implement the requested behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's addGuestStudents method match the specification by changing its signature to addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update the implementation to accept and (optionally) record or use the reason. Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unused, update the problem statement and UML to reflect the single-parameter signature so all artifacts remain consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task description) specifies a method addGuestStudents(int, String) that accepts a number of new guest students and a reason, but the solution implements addGuestStudents(int) with only a single int parameter. This mismatch between the expected method signature and the provided implementation can confuse students mapping the task requirements to the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the problem specification: change the solution (and template) method signature to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) and update the implementation to accept and (optionally) record or use the reason parameter. Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unused, update the problem statement/UML to require only addGuestStudents(int) so all artifacts match.
